phase1.name: Phase 1 — simple database-backed role authorization
phase1.approval: User accepted the simplified first phase on 13 November 2026; this revision changes contract/docs/checks, not application behavior or deployed data.
phase1.precedence: Overrides earlier session, role-policy editing and password-workflow decisions only for Phase 1; unrelated booking, privacy, concurrency and reporting rules remain.
phase1.authentication: Bearer-only signed access JWT; no authentication cookies, CSRF bootstrap, refresh, stored login session, renewal or role/password gates.
phase1.tokenLifetime: Required positive finite server configuration; fixed per issuance, no sliding renewal. No new numeric lifetime is selected here. accessExpiresAt is authoritative. The former five-minute-plus-refresh rule is deferred.
phase1.storage: Browser memory only; reload/expiry requires login. No persistent browser storage or token URL.
phase1.logout: Local token/user/private-cache clearing only; no logout HTTP endpoint and no per-token revocation claim. Copies remain usable until expiry while the account is active.
phase1.currentAuthority: Read current active employee, exactly one assigned fixed role and active PA official assignments on every protected request; repeat resource/assignment checks in write transactions. JWT role/permission claims and browser hints are never authority.
phase1.manualAdministration: Provision accounts with encoded bcrypt credentials and exactly one role_pegawai row; initial Super Admin is assigned the same way. PA assignments use pegawai_pejabat. Existing multiple-role accounts need deliberate manual selection before Phase 1 login; never pick/union silently.
phase1.employeeUI: Employee directory/detail are read-only; account creation/editing, role tags, assignment editing and role-policy UI are deferred.
phase1.permissionSource: Fixed backend mapping from the existing frontend role vocabulary, with roles/audit-only administration removed from Phase 1; database policy graph is not read or exposed.
basicsRetained: Password hashing and generic credential failures
Input validation, basic login throttling and existing public/staff request budgets
HTTPS for non-loopback deployment; explicit browser-origin policy
Ordinary/restricted privacy boundaries and public code/email proof
